content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Has anyone had recent experience with dimming light circuits via a [product_name]? I'm aiming to set up a soft start function and control security/mood lighting at full or reduced output (such as 100% or 30-50%). I'm considering the use of a transformer output unit to drive solid state relays with a PWM signal, but I'm unsure if this would result in flickering. I found a related thread at [url], but the links are no longer active. The 0-10V dimmers I located seem tailored for fluorescent or HID lamps, whereas I need a solution for incandescent and 240V halogen lamps. Any advice would be appreciated.
Has no one tried this approach yet?

I suggest looking into a 0-10V interface specifically designed for halogen lighting. There are also similar interfaces available for incandescent lights. You can check the Osram site for details. Note that solid state relays might have insufficient switching speed. For example, if you utilize 50% of the sinewave beginning at zero crossing, you would need to activate for 4 ms out of every 8 ms.
Thanks for your suggestion. Do you happen to recall the exact model name or number? The link you provided seems to return an error.
It's listed on the Osram website under professional products, ECG & LMS, electronic controls for low voltage halogen lamps. The model number I found is: HT 1-10/230-240 DIM FS1. Hope that helps,
Understood, thank you very much for your assistance.

There is concern regarding flicker when using solid state relays with PWM, and some technical resources are now inaccessible, prompting users to seek current recommendations and proven approaches.
